title: Data agent configurations - Microsoft Fabric | Microsoft Learn
summary: Microsoft Learn's concept article enumerating the four configuration surfaces available when curating a Fabric data agent — agent-level instructions, per-data-source instructions, data source descriptions, and example queries — including a recommended template structure for each and how the agent actually consumes example queries at answer time.
audience: Data agent creators and content curators who need a structured approach to prompt/instruction authoring rather than ad hoc trial and error.
why_it_matters: Because a data agent's routing and query-generation quality is driven entirely by these four configuration layers rather than any per-tenant model tuning, this page is the practical playbook for making an agent behave like a subject-matter expert on a specific dataset instead of a generic text-to-SQL tool.
takeaways: There are four distinct, independently editable configuration surfaces: agent-level instructions, data-source-level instructions, data source descriptions, and data-source example queries.
Agent-level instructions are best structured with sections for objective, prioritized data sources, key terminology, response guidelines, and handling of common topics.
Data source descriptions are what the agent's routing logic actually reads to decide which attached source is relevant to a given question.
Example queries aren't just stored as reference text — at answer time the system automatically retrieves the top three most relevant examples for the current question and feeds them into generation.
The configuration model treats curation as an ongoing content task (writing and refining instructions/descriptions/examples), not a one-time setup step.

claims.text: A Fabric data agent exposes four distinct configuration surfaces that together shape its behavior: agent-level instructions, data-source-level instructions, data source descriptions, and data-source example queries.

Agent-level instructions operate above any single data source and are meant to state the agent's overall objective, set a priority order across attached data sources, define key terminology/acronyms, and specify response-formatting expectations.

Data-source-level instructions apply only once the agent has already routed a question to a specific source, and are meant to hold source-specific guidance such as relevant tables, columns, relationships, and query logic needed for common or complex questions.

A data source description is a separate, high-level summary of what a given attached source contains and what kinds of questions it can answer, and the agent uses this description as one of its inputs when deciding which source is relevant to a given user question.
The routing decision for which data source to use factors in each source's description, schema, and example queries together, not any single signal in isolation.

Data source example queries are a few-shot mechanism: when a data source is selected for a question, its tool automatically looks up the most relevant example queries and passes the top three into the query-generation step.

The recommended agent-level instructions template is organized into named sections — Objective, Data sources, Key terminology, Response guidelines, and Handling common topics — as a starting structure for authors rather than free-form prose.
The recommended data-source-instructions template is organized into General knowledge, Table descriptions, and When asked about sections, distinct from the agent-level template.
